justification_text:
My point estimates for the underlying asset showed a slight but consistent upward trend across the different time horizons, starting at 135.56 for one day, rising to 135.75 for one week, and reaching 136.53 for one month. This progression suggests that my forecast incorporated an expectation of modest positive momentum or a gradual appreciation over time, perhaps driven by an underlying fundamental analysis or a general market trend that I anticipate will continue. The immediate 1-day estimate was likely heavily influenced by very recent price action and prevailing market sentiment, while the longer-term estimates allowed for a bit more time for these underlying positive drivers to manifest, leading to the slightly higher projected values.

The widening of the 90% confidence intervals for each subsequent horizon reflects the inherent increase in uncertainty as we look further into the future. For the 1-day forecast, the interval was relatively tight, ranging from 131.65 to 139.54, primarily accounting for typical daily market fluctuations and minor news. As we extend to one week, the interval broadened significantly to [127.12, 144.75], and even more so to [119.17, 155.4] for the one-month period. This expansion acknowledges that over longer durations, more unpredictable factors come into play, such as broader economic data releases, company-specific announcements, shifts in sector trends, or changes in overall market sentiment, all of which introduce greater variability into potential outcomes.

Specific risks or events that could push outcomes outside these stated intervals are typically those high-impact, low-probability occurrences that are difficult to model within standard forecasting frameworks. On the downside, unexpected severe economic downturns, major geopolitical crises, a sudden and significant negative company-specific event like a product recall, a legal scandal, or a massive earnings miss could drive the value well below the lower bound of the one-month interval. Conversely, a breakthrough technological innovation, a highly successful new product launch exceeding all expectations, an unexpected merger or acquisition at a significant premium, or a sudden, favorable shift in regulatory policy could propel the value far above the upper bound. These "black swan" type events represent the primary threats to the accuracy of even wide confidence intervals.
